report:
Independently inspected the fresh claim, both implementation entries, and both complete annotated tests from review start. Captured the containing solver model with review read. This is a source review; no tests were executed in this refresh, and root owns centralized execution. No source edits were made.

Requirements considered: one final output per frame; one owned producer for its canonical atomic query and shared subscriptions; revisioned candidate/frame side progress without extra future outputs or raw candidate exposure; Rust-future continuations with bounded polling rounds. The ordinary solve_query association captures prove.rs, including all whiteboard internals and the substantive test setup. Whiteboard::request reuses a frame by (query,parent,remaining_depth), creates a fresh subscription for pending work, and guards producer creation with producer_started and a single optional producer slot. Each producer owns its query and awaits solve_atomic_frame before returning its single (FrameId, Stashed<QueryResult>) output. complete requires Pending, stores Ready once, drains subscriptions and wakes waiters. ProofFuture::poll yields Pending while remembering the requester waker, or clones the final result; ready cache requests use immediate results. No subscription API exposes a candidate state or a progress output. ProducerFuture and prove_goal are pinned Rust futures, so suspended work is not reified into a separate continuation interpreter. Candidate processing remains internal to the producer; this assessment of the output boundary does not assert correctness of the separate unification, canonicalization or answer-reduction algorithms.

The ordinary same_parent_requests_share_one_live_producer_and_result test visibly constructs an atomic bool-equality query, creates two pending requests in the same context, asserts equal frame identity and two subscribers, drives both futures and asserts equal results. A later request must use the immediate cached result, equal to the original. It then asserts one frame, Ready state and no subscriptions. These assertions detect duplicate frames, divergent responses and incomplete subscriber cleanup. The with_crate/make_test_crate/equality_query setup helpers are all present in the initial whole-file snapshot, and contain setup rather than hidden behavioral assertions. This is meaningful coverage of the implemented shared-final-result subset.

The second implementation entry and solver_shared_final_result test are explicitly TODO. Their explanation defers bounded polling rounds and monotone intermediate publication. Current ProofFrame contains terminal state and subscriptions but no revisioned progress channel, and Whiteboard::drive drains the ready queue without a per-round bound. These requirements are not implemented by the mere use of Future. The TODO test has no assertions and is not counted as verification: it specifies remaining progress snapshots, candidate-local non-observation and self-waking fairness scenarios. Implementing the revisioned progress channel and bounded-round scheduling is the prerequisite for those tests; dedicated observation tests must then exercise that channel without exposing raw candidate state. Existing duplicate-request coverage now satisfies that portion of its broader intended matrix. The deferral remains visible and accepted as planned work, consistent with the containing solver model explicitly identifying scheduling as planned. No N/A evidence is present.

All requirements are accounted for by the implemented terminal-publication structure and substantive test, or the explicit justified TODO implementation/test evidence. No new behavioral concern or required source change was found in this refresh. Acceptance does not promote the deferred scheduling/progress behavior to implemented status.
